match.reason: The bank point describes Australia's health status and the rise of chronic disease, not the biomedical approach of treating disease once it occurs, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: The biomedical approach
card: The biomedical approach to health focuses on treating disease and injury once they have occurred. It sees ill health as a problem in the body that can be diagnosed and fixed.
It relies on doctors, hospitals, medical technology and medicine. Examples include surgery, antibiotics, scans and chemotherapy.
Its strength is that it saves lives and restores health. Many people with serious illness or injury recover because of it.
Its limits are cost and timing. Treatment and equipment are expensive, and care usually starts after a person is already ill, so it does little to prevent illness.
draft.remember: Biomedical means treating illness after it starts: it saves lives but costs a lot and prevents little.

a.q: Which action is an example of the biomedical approach?
opts: A surgeon removes a tumour from a patient
A council builds a bike path in a new suburb
A school runs a program on healthy lunches
A workplace lets staff choose flexible hours
a.why: Surgery treats a disease in the body after it has occurred, using a doctor and technology. The bike path is tempting because it helps health, but it aims to stop illness before it starts, which is not the focus of the biomedical approach.
a.clue: Look for the one that treats an illness already present.

b.q: A hospital in Geelong buys a new scanner that finds cancers and guides treatment. Why is this mainly a biomedical response, not a way to prevent illness?
opts: It diagnoses and treats disease after it has developed
It changes the living conditions that cause disease
It teaches people how to avoid risk factors for cancer
It lowers costs because fewer people need treatment
b.why: The scanner works on people who already have disease, so it is treatment, not prevention. The cost option is wrong because the biomedical approach is costly, and new technology adds to that cost.
b.clue: Ask when in the course of illness the scanner is used.

a.best: A surgeon removes a tumour from a patient

b.best: It diagnoses and treats disease after it has developed
